report:
Reviewed the complete expansion_import_ambiguity claim, all three implementation associations, and all ten ordinary annotated tests. No TODO/N/A entries apply. The claim concerns final validation of unqualified import roots, not a new macro-expansion scheduling algorithm or arbitrary hygiene semantics.

Implementation: Resolver::import_root_is_expansion_ambiguous accepts only relative paths, uses the type namespace for intermediate roots, and holds the root query in flight while resolving import edges. It separately collects generated named bindings and glob bindings, reporting a conflict only when both buckets reach distinct Symbol identities. NamedLookup::Generated uses the binding item span: source-written aliases to generated definitions are therefore correctly excluded. The associated symbol_local_item helper covers supported local named item kinds; captured LocalModItemSym::absolute_span routes each to its own span. Bang and derive parse sources count as generated. Existing macro-expansion lookup still combines named and glob candidates; normal lookup retains precedence. Definition deduplication in resolve_name_from_module prevents repeated routes from becoming multiple candidates.

LocalUseSym::diagnostics performs the audit for every flattened import before ordinary resolution, selects Type alone for glob targets and all importable namespaces for terminal named imports, and emits one relative-span error then continues. Captured compile/observe.rs shows the whole-crate consumer explicitly demands import diagnostics, including unused imports. The associated mods.rs fixed-point expanded item query exposes generated items before the normal-mode audit. The additional span and observer fragments are supporting dependencies; the three associated files contain the new validation algorithm, origin classification, and import entrypoint.

Tests: generated_module_competes_with_glob_import_path checks the original unused-import discrepancy with one shared ERROR marker and the exact Sage diagnostic snapshot. generated_named_import_competes_with_glob_root exercises a generated use binding, and ambiguous_root_of_longer_import_is_rejected verifies a multi-segment root. nested_expansion_competes_with_glob_root and generated_import_and_binding_in_same_expansion_conflict cover nested provenance and a generated import, including invocation-site diagnostic matching. generated_named_import_and_glob_can_reach_same_definition ensures duplicate routes are accepted and the resulting Item type is usable. qualified_glob_path_selects_generated_module checks explicit crate anchoring; source_written_module_takes_precedence_over_glob and source_written_alias_to_generated_module_keeps_precedence check source-origin precedence while confirming the selected field type. glob_root_ignores_conflicting_value_namespace_bindings protects against auditing an irrelevant namespace for a glob target. Positive fixtures omit diagnostic expectations, requiring no errors; negative fixtures require exactly the declared error. The captured prepare method unconditionally runs rustc and requires both compiler results before success, so the shared markers are differential acceptance/location evidence rather than Sage-only assertions.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test macro_glob_paths with updating disabled: all 10 tests passed, zero ignored/failed. Existing compiler warnings were nonfatal. This review does not claim broader Rust macro conformance, which lies outside this narrow anchor. Source inspection and these assertions account for every qualification in the claim; no edits requested.
